component.name: prev
component.summary: View, mark up and sign PDFs and images

description.p: prev is a fast document and image viewer and editor, similar to macOS Preview. It opens PDFs, images, camera RAW photos, SVG drawings and Markdown, and edits them in place.

ul.li: Read PDFs with continuous, single and two-page layouts, sharp at any zoom, with search, a table of contents, thumbnails and bookmarks
Mark up with Preview's tools: highlights, drawing, shapes, text boxes, notes and signatures, saved as standard annotations
Fill in forms, sign documents, and redact content for good
Reorder, rotate, insert, delete, crop and merge pages, and export to PDF or images
Edit photos: rotate, flip, crop, resize and adjust color, keeping their metadata, and mark them up
Drag and drop, copy and paste with other apps both ways
Autosave with versions kept, Material 3 design, and colors from the system accent color

screenshot.caption: A form filled in, marked up and signed
Adjusting the color of a photo

description.p: Parts of a text box's text can be bold, italic or in a color of their own, saved as PDF rich text. The assistant sends the model much less with each request and summarizes long chats before they outgrow a local model's context. On Linux desktops that draw no title bars, such as Hyprland, the toolbar ends with a button that closes the window. prev now starts on a Windows without the Visual C++ Redistributable, and the text box editor lines up with the page.
The names and descriptions of prev's tools, which the assistant and outside agents read, are now in US English like the rest of the interface.
The Windows installer and program are now signed by Scramble Tools LLC, so Windows names the publisher rather than warning of an unknown one.

Menus have a new look: the markup bar's style menus show headings, round color swatches and size and alignment buttons, saved signatures appear as pictures, and drop-downs stay plain until pointed at. Drawn signatures now taper as the pen lifts, Markdown text can fill the window for wide tables and long lines, and buttons beside text fields line up with them.

Markup feels like a drawing app: dragging a handle shows the annotation as it will be, with lines keeping their width and text boxes rewrapping, dragging past the edge scrolls the page, a loupe shows what is under it as it moves, notes can be dragged, and every shape is framed by its own outline. The assistant now opens where the inspector does and takes its place, and does what you ask it without asking again, the toolbar no longer shifts as the markup bar opens, and the pointer stays the plain arrow except to resize, select text and draw.

prev now has an assistant: a chat panel beside the document that answers about the file and works in it, finding and pointing at things, marking up, filling in, editing, signing and redacting, asking first where you choose. It talks to a local model, such as Ollama's, or to a cloud model from Anthropic, OpenAI or Google with your API key, kept in the system keychain. AI agents such as Claude Code can also control prev over MCP. Also: Settings in tabs, colors that follow the system accent as it changes, toolbars matching the title bar on Windows and macOS, and bold text drawn in prev's own font.

Drag and drop now works both ways on macOS. Images dropped on the page thumbnails, or dragged there from a page, become pages of their own, a PDF dropped on a page asks whether to add it to the end, and holding Ctrl sends a drop to the sidebar. Colors now follow the system accent color on Windows, macOS and Linux desktops, or a color picked in Settings, and Ctrl+drag pans a zoomed-in document. Also: animated images no longer flicker, notices go away after 10 seconds, and closing the file chooser no longer shows an error.

The interface now comes in 38 languages, adding Bengali, Catalan, Czech, Finnish, Greek, Hungarian, Indonesian, Malay, Norwegian, European Portuguese, Romanian, Swahili, Swedish, Tamil, Thai, Urdu and Vietnamese. Urdu is laid out right to left.

Keyboard shortcuts can be changed in the settings file, a Settings button makes prev the default app for its file types, and a selected annotation shows a crisp box with square handles. HEIC and AVIF now open on every Mac, and Windows ships one smaller library for them.

prev now runs on macOS on Apple Silicon, and its interface comes in 21 languages, laid out right to left for Arabic, Hebrew and Persian. Also: an input language setting, prev's version in Settings, and fixes for the floating toolbar and two-page view.
Showing or hiding the markup bar no longer scrolls back to the top, and images keep their zoom and position when markup opens or closes.
prev is now built for ARM64 on Linux and Windows, and for RISC-V on Linux.

prev now runs on Windows. Markdown gets a toolbar with text size, search, an inspector and export as a picture; image and SVG export ask their choices in prev's own dialog; the mouse wheel scrolls smoothly.
